r3_a_arm_fm_djepa_eps4.change: fm_djepa (sha d3e82576...) with EPS 0.2 -> 4.0 and manifest epsilon 4.0; nothing else
r3_a_arm_fm_djepa_eps4.note: base = -(distance rank)/(K-1) spans [0, 1], so at epsilon 4 the bounded claim no longer constrains the ordering. V1 still checks |score - base| <= 4 + 1e-5, and passing it says nothing: this arm is a D-JEPA-shaped free ranker, not a bounded corrector. The key exists so that no epsilon-0.2 result is ever reported under this arm's number or vice versa.

r3_b_arm_ch_dj_stoch_noLN.hypothesis: LayerNorm over a 2-vector (a, b) returns (+-1, -+1) * (a - b)/|a - b| (up to eps): one sign bit. Magnitude and direction of the predicted latent are destroyed before the encoder, so only the distance rank r (computed before the LN) survives, and the arm sits at the latent-distance floor.
r3_b_arm_ch_dj_stoch_noLN.hypothesis_kill: noLN hit_shuffled < best floor + 0.02 on >= 2 of the 3 draws: the LN is not what holds the arm at floor

r3_c_replication.draw_means: a draw is the verifier tag every secret_seed of the ranker path derives from: the 4 run seeds (r2_c rule), train/eval sets, the secret shuffle, the V1 probes and the null labels. Different tags are independent sha256(salt|tag|...) draws. Tags are public, seeds are not.
r3_c_replication.rule: PASS_V2 (or PASS_V3) counts only if it holds on >= 3 independent draws; one draw is anecdote. m0 is draw 1 (the r2 verdicts); fm_resolvent and fm_hop1 run r3d1 and r3d2; fm_djepa_eps4 and ch_dj_stoch_noLN run all three.
r3_c_replication.caching_fix: verifier._RFLOOR was keyed by bed only, so a second draw in one process would have been scored against the first draw's floors; r3 keys it by (bed, tag). Registered here as part of the replication instrument.

r3_d_ranker_v3.pool_source: controls/<name>/candidate.py, verifier-owned. r_pool_point = byte copy of candidates_rjepa/fm_point (Foreman's pointwise Head, H 63); r_pool_djepa02 = byte copy of candidates_rjepa/fm_djepa (Foreman's D-JEPA Head, H 24, epsilon 0.2).
r3_d_ranker_v3.read: after V2 passes, each pool member runs the SAME sandbox job as the candidate (same draw, run seeds, data, schedule, budget); its score is its pooled secret-shuffle hit. margin = candidate hit_shuffled - max pool hit. REJECT V3 (L-BR) if margin < 0.02.
r3_d_ranker_v3.why_0_02: the operator V3 margin (bars.json addendum_1 v3_margin) and the ranker V2 floor margin are both 0.02; pooled N = 16,000 eval sets per draw puts one hit's SE near 0.0038
r3_d_ranker_v3.disclosed_pilot: m0 numbers were known before this key: r2 fm_djepa (= r_pool_djepa02) 0.3489, fm_hop1 0.3603, fm_resolvent 0.3770. On m0, 0.02 is expected to reject fm_hop1 at V3 (margin ~0.011) and pass fm_resolvent (~0.028). The margin was not chosen for that outcome; it is the house's existing number.
r3_d_ranker_v3.pool_integrity: a pool member that errors or is rejected at an integrity stage on a draw raises InfraError: ERROR, never a verdict
r3_d_ranker_v3.verdict: PASS_V3 = cleared V0, V1, V4, V2, V3; no V5 ladder is registered for rankers, so still never ACCEPT

r3_d_ranker_v3.v2_hole_disclosed: the label-shuffle null is built second in the runner process; build order is observable, so a candidate can sandbag its own null and lower its V2 line (m0: best floor would fall from ~0.33 to latent_distance 0.3223). V2 is not changed this round; V3's verifier-owned pool is what catches r06. Route: run the null in its own sandbox process with the same build index as a real run.
